title: Part Four, Chapter 5: The Farewell of the First Fathers

verses.t: And when they knew that they were dying, they gave notice to their sons. And they were not sick, nor were they in the throes of death, when they disposed of their affairs and gave notice to their sons. And these were the names of their sons. Balam-quitzé had two: the first was called Gocaib, and the second Gocavib, who are the fathers and grandfathers of the people of Caviquib. And Balam-acab had two other sons, and they were called thus: the first Goacul, and the second son of Balam-acab was called Goacutec. And Mahucutah begot only one, who was called Gohaan. And only these three had sons; and truly they were lords worthy of respect. And these were the names of the sons, and to these they gave their counsel and commands, all four of them together. And they sang, and were sad, and wept in their song; and the song was called Gamagú; that was the name of the song they sang. And then they counselled their sons: "Look, our sons! We are going, and we shall not come back. And this word and command that we give you now is illustrious and clear. It is not long since you came from that homeland of yours, which is far away. You, our wives," they said to their wives (and they took leave of each one separately), "we are going to our town. The Lord of the Deer is already set in order; he is plain to see in the sky. Now we shall make our return; all that was in our charge has been done; our days are complete. Do not forget us, nor lose us. Look after your houses and your homeland, and settle and multiply; and come and go back to see again the place we came from." This is what they said when they took their leave. And then there was left a sign of the being and the custom of Balam-quitzé, and he said to them, "This I leave you, so that you will remember us; this I leave with you, and this shall be your greatness. I have taken my leave and counselled you, and I am sad." This is what he said when he left them the sign of his being and custom, which is called the Bundled Majesty and Greatness. And it is not known what it is, for it remained wrapped up and was never untied or unwrapped; and it is not known where it is sewn, because they did not see it when it was wrapped. And such was their leave-taking; and they vanished from the top of the mountain Hacavitz, and they were seen no more by their wives or sons; and it is not known what became of them when they disappeared. Only their leave-taking was known, and the bundle, which was a thing much loved by them. And this was the memorial of their fathers; and then they burned offerings before the memorial of their fathers. And from here men were born through the lords, when they took from Balam-quitzé; the fathers and grandfathers of the people of Caviquib began, and his sons Gocaib and Gocavib were not lost. And such were the deaths of those four, our first fathers and grandfathers, when they disappeared and left their sons on the mountain Hacavitz. And their sons stayed there; and once the peoples were subjugated, they no longer had greatness, but stayed there and bore their burdens every day, and remembered their fathers. And that bundle was a great thing to them, and they did not untie it, but it stayed wrapped up with them; and it is called by them the Bundled Greatness. And then what their father had given them to keep was celebrated and given its name, only in memory of who they were, when they did it. And so it was when Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam disappeared and were lost: the first men who came from the other side of the sea, from the East. Long ago they came here, and they are dead now, having lived to be very old; and they are called the Respected and Revered Ones.
